Class QueueRefs

java.lang.Object
threepl.exec.QueueRefs
All Implemented Interfaces:
TDEConstants, Constant
public class QueueRefs extends Object implements Constant, TDEConstants
This class represents a collection of queue references. It is used in the generation of queue acknowledgements. Queue availability may be conditional on a signal; the test operand for a ?: operator or a selection input to a select() function.

Field 'write_queues' is a (possibly empty) set containing the queue variables (Var) whose write availability is required. This is used by sync{}. Field 'read_queues' is a (possibly empty) set containing the queue variables (Var) whose read availability is required. This is used by sync{}.

Field 'read_ands' is a set of queues and conditional signals which are all to be used to form availability and acknowledge expressions. This field is a set of set pairs, the pair being a queue variable set and a conditional signal set. For each set entry the queue and signal sets are all ANDed together to form one term. The terms for each position in the lists are ORed together. Sets are used for the queues and signals to be ANDed to avoid duplicate entries.

When a write queue is ANDed to this queue reference by method 'and_set' it is added to the 'write_queues' set.

When a read queue is ANDed to this queue reference by method 'and_set' it is added to the 'read_queues' set. If set 'read_ands' is empty the queue is added as a new pair otherwise it is added to every queue set in list 'read_ands'.

When a conditional signal is ANDed to this queue reference by method 'and' it is added to every signal set in list 'read_ands'.

When another queue reference is ANDed to this queue reference by method 'and_set', if this queue reference 'read_ands' set is not empty the product of the two queue references is generated by taking each combination of list indices from each queue reference and taking a union of the sets. If this queue reference 'read_ands' set is empty the queue reference is copied.

When another queue reference is ORed to this queue reference by method 'or' the lists are appended.

This process of multiplying through each time means that we maintain the queue dependencies as a sum of products, no deeper.

    • setReadAVCheck

      public void setReadAVCheck(QueueRefs pr)
      Set the read availability check set from a queues reference. The set will be empty prior to this - this method is only called at one place in nodes/ExprNode.java when evaluating the queue read availability operator and the class is newly constructed prior to the call. Queues from both the argument write availability check set and the argument write queues set are added.
      Parameters:
      pr - is the queues reference

    • getSyncAvail

      public Val getSyncAvail(Scope module_scope, QueueRefs checkedqueues, SrcLoc loc)
      Get the sync block availability signal for this queues reference, or null. If there are no queue references null is returned. Note that the queue availability does not include any conditional signals (from queues in the 2nd or 3rd arguments of a ?: operator). This is only called in one place - nodes/SyncBlock.execute() calls codegen/TDEList.execp() which calls exec/Queue.syncAvail() which calls exec/QueueRefs.getSyncAvail().
      Parameters:
      module_scope - is the scope we are in
      checkedqueues - lists queues that need not be checked for availability
      loc - is the source file location
      Returns:
      the availability value

    • getRAvail

      public Val getRAvail(Scope module_scope, SrcLoc loc)
      Get the read availability signal for a '<' operator for this queues reference. This is only called from one place in method getReadAvailVal() in exec/Val.java which in turn is called from nodes/ExprNode.java when evaluating the read availability operator.
      Parameters:
      module_scope - is the scope we are in
      loc - is the source file location
      Returns:
      the availability value

      Parameters:

    • unbufferedQueues

      public boolean unbufferedQueues(boolean allow_one, String mess, SrcLoc loc)
      Examine an instance of the class for queues of zero depth, i.e. unbuffered. If there are no unbuffered queues then false is returned. If allow_one is true and there is a single unbuffered queue then true is returned. If allow_one is true and there is more than one unbuffered queue an exception is thrown using the message argument.
      Parameters:
      allow_one - if true directs that one unbuffered queue is allowed
      mess - is an error message string
      loc - is a source file location
      Returns:
      true if there is an unbuffered queue and it is allowed
